entities.name: Leishmaniasis
entities.description: A complex vector-borne protozoal infection caused by obligate intracellular parasites of the genus Leishmania, presenting across three distinct clinical syndromes: visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar, characterized by prolonged undulating fever, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, hypergammaglobulinemia, and high fatality if untreated), cutaneous leishmaniasis (indolent volcano-like crusted ulcers with preserved local sensation), and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (destructive naso-oropharyngeal cartilage erosion).

entities.name: Phlebotomine Sandfly Bite
entities.description: Inoculation by the bite of tiny (1.5-3 mm), silent, non-buzzing female phlebotomine sandflies (genus Phlebotomus in Old World arid zones and Mediterranean; genus Lutzomyia in New World tropical rainforests) that bite predominantly from dusk to dawn and breed in organic debris, rodent burrows, termite mounds, and cracked mud walls.

entities.name: Endemic Visceral Leishmaniasis Geographic Exposure in South Asia and East Africa
entities.description: Residence in or travel to high-burden rural anthroponotic visceral leishmaniasis foci, including the Gangetic plains of Eastern India (Bihar, West Bengal), Bangladesh, Nepal, and East African savannah regions (Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya).

entities.name: Zoonotic Canine Reservoir Exposure in the Mediterranean Basin and Latin America
entities.description: Domestic and stray dog reservoir exposure maintaining transmission of zoonotic Leishmania infantum (chagasi) via phlebotomine sandfly vectors in peri-urban and rural areas of the Mediterranean basin, Middle East, Central Asia, and Latin America (predominantly Brazil).

entities.name: Sylvatic Forest Rodent and Marsupial Habitat Exposure in Latin America
entities.description: Occupational or environmental exposure within tropical rainforest ecosystems (affecting gum tree harvesters, loggers, military personnel, and eco-tourists) inhabited by wild rodent and marsupial reservoirs harboring New World Leishmania species.

entities.name: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Co-Infection and Cellular Immunosuppression
entities.description: Profound defect in host cell-mediated immunity (CD4+ T-cell depletion in HIV/AIDS, organ transplantation, chemotherapy, or severe malnutrition) that accelerates the progression of asymptomatic Leishmania infection to full-blown visceral disease, atypical multisystem involvement, frequent relapses, and high mortality.

entities.name: Leishmania donovani Species Complex
entities.description: Obligate intracellular dimorphic protozoan parasite multiplying as aflagellated amastigotes inside host mononuclear phagocytes, causing anthroponotic visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) and post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) in South Asia and East Africa.

entities.name: Leishmania infantum (syn. Leishmania chagasi)
entities.description: Obligate intracellular protozoan belonging to the Leishmania donovani complex that causes zoonotic visceral leishmaniasis in infants, young children, and immunocompromised adults across the Mediterranean basin, Middle East, and Latin America.

entities.name: Leishmania braziliensis Complex
entities.description: Aggressive protozoan parasite belonging to the Viannia subgenus that causes New World cutaneous leishmaniasis with high propensity for late hematogenous or lymphatic metastatic dissemination to the naso-oropharyngeal mucosa (mucocutaneous leishmaniasis / Espundia).

entities.name: Leishmania mexicana Complex
entities.description: New World protozoan pathogen responsible for localized cutaneous leishmaniasis, chronic destructive chiclero's ulcer of the ear pinna cartilage, and anergic diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis in Central and South America.

entities.name: Leishmania major and Leishmania tropica
entities.description: Old World protozoan parasites responsible for zoonotic (L. major) and anthroponotic (L. tropica) localized cutaneous leishmaniasis (oriental sore) characterized by self-limiting or chronic crusted dermal ulcers in the Middle East, North Africa, and Central Asia.

entities.name: Massive Non-Tender Splenomegaly
entities.description: Progressive, massive enlargement of the spleen, which becomes firm, hard, non-tender, and often extends down below the umbilicus into the right iliac fossa or pelvic brim, reflecting intense reticuloendothelial hyperplasia and parasite sequestration.

entities.name: Double-Spiking Daily Fever Curve (Dromedary Fever)
entities.description: Chronic, undulating or spiking remittent fever classically displaying two distinct temperature spikes within a 24-hour cycle ('dromedary curve'), accompanied by chills, drenching night sweats, and absence of severe toxic prostration corresponding to fever magnitude.

entities.name: Profound Cachexia with Ashen Cutaneous Hyperpigmentation
entities.description: Severe progressive wasting, marked temporal hollowing, prominent ribs, protuberant abdomen, and grayish-black hyperpigmentation noticeable on the forehead, temples, perioral skin, hands, and abdomen (giving rise to the Hindi name Kala-Azar or 'black fever').

entities.name: Volcano-Like Painless Cutaneous Ulcer with Raised Indurated Border
entities.description: Indolent, painless dermal ulcer with sharply demarcated, elevated, violaceous, indurated rolled margins and an adherent central crusted necrotic crater oozing serous exudate, with completely intact local sensory innervation.

entities.name: Destructive Mucocutaneous Granulomatous Ulceration with Tapir-Face Deformity
entities.description: Metastatic granulomatous destruction of the cartilaginous nasal septum, nasal columella, palate, pharynx, and larynx, resulting in septal perforation, nasal collapse, and classical 'tapir face' (espundia) disfigurement.

entities.name: Chiclero's Auricular Chondral Ulcer
entities.description: Chronic, mutilating necrotizing ulceration involving the helix and anti-helix of the ear pinna caused by Leishmania mexicana, leading to severe erosion and permanent notch-like defects of the auricular cartilage.

entities.name: Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL)
entities.description: Dermatological complication developing months to years following visceral leishmaniasis cure, presenting as hypopigmented macules that evolve into non-ulcerating erythematous papules, plaques, and nodules teeming with amastigotes on the face, trunk, and limbs, serving as an infectious reservoir.

entities.name: Pancytopenia with Severe Leukopenia, Anemia, and Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Concurrent admission depression of all three peripheral hematologic lineages: normocytic normochromic anemia (hemoglobin often < 7-8 g/dL), profound leukopenia (WBC < 2,500-3,500/uL with absolute neutrophil count < 1,000/uL), and marked thrombocytopenia (platelets < 50,000-80,000/uL), driven by bone marrow reticuloendothelial replacement and splenic pooling.

entities.name: Marked Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia with Reversed Albumin-to-Globulin Ratio
entities.description: Intense polyclonal B-cell activation driving astronomical serum IgG levels, elevating total serum protein (> 9-11 g/dL) while serum albumin is severely depressed (< 2.5 g/dL), producing a characteristic reversed Albumin-to-Globulin (A:G) ratio (< 0.5).

entities.name: Intracellular Leishman-Donovan Amastigote Bodies in Macrophages
entities.description: Microscopic identification on Giemsa- or Wright-stained smears of splenic aspirate (>95% sensitivity), bone marrow aspirate (70-85% sensitivity), lymph node aspirate, or dermal scraping showing round-to-oval 2-4 um aflagellated amastigotes containing a purplish nucleus and a perpendicular rod-shaped kinetoplast inside histiocytes.

entities.name: Positive Recombinant Kinesin Antigen rK39 Immunochromatographic Dipstick
entities.description: Point-of-care rapid diagnostic serological test detecting circulating antibodies directed against the 39-amino-acid repeat of Leishmania donovani kinesin-related protein, offering >98% sensitivity and specificity in immunocompetent patients in South Asia (lower sensitivity ~85% in East Africa).

entities.name: Homogeneous Splenomegaly and Hepatomegaly on Bedside Ultrasound
entities.description: Abdominal ultrasonography demonstrating massive splenomegaly with homogeneous parenchymal echotexture and smooth hepatomegaly, while definitively confirming the absence of focal abscesses, cysts, biliary obstruction, or periportal fibrosis.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/uL)
entities.description: Leukocyte count exceeding 15,000/uL with pronounced absolute neutrophilia, which strongly argues against uncomplicated visceral leishmaniasis, an illness consistently defined by reticuloendothelial bone marrow infiltration and severe neutropenic leukopenia.

entities.name: Loss of Thermal or Pinprick Sensation within Cutaneous Skin Lesion
entities.description: Hypoesthesia or complete anesthesia to fine touch, pinprick, or thermal stimuli within a dermatological plaque or ulcer, which excludes cutaneous leishmaniasis (where local cutaneous sensation remains strictly preserved) and indicates tuberculoid leprosy.

entities.name: Circulating Leukemic Blast Cells on Peripheral Blood Smear or Bone Marrow
entities.description: Identification of immature myeloid or lymphoid blast cells (>20% in marrow or prominent in peripheral blood), which establishes a primary hematologic malignancy (acute myeloid/lymphoblastic leukemia) as the etiology of pancytopenia and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Periportal Pipestem Fibrosis and Schistosoma Eggs on Microscopic Stool Exam
entities.description: Demonstration of periportal 'pipestem' (Symmers) fibrosis on liver ultrasonography along with viable lateral-spined Schistosoma mansoni ova in stool or rectal biopsy, which excludes visceral leishmaniasis in a patient presenting with splenomegaly and portal hypertension.

entities.name: Intraerythrocytic Plasmodium Ring Trophozoites on Blood Smear with Indirect Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Identification of intraerythrocytic ring-stage malaria parasites on Giemsa-stained thin/thick blood films alongside unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, cyclic rigors, and rapid clinical resolution following artemisinin-combination therapy.

entities.name: Hyperreactive Malarial Splenomegaly (HMS)
entities.description: Chronic immunological disorder secondary to recurrent malaria characterized by massive splenomegaly, marked polyclonal IgM elevation, and responsiveness to antimalarial chemoprophylaxis; differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis by absence of severe leukopenia, lack of amastigotes on marrow aspirate, and negative rK39 testing.

entities.name: Hepatosplenic Schistosomiasis
entities.description: Chronic helminthic granulomatous disease caused by Schistosoma mansoni or S. japonicum causing presinusoidal portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and splenomegaly; differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis by afebrile course, preserved bone marrow hematopoiesis (normal leukocyte counts), periportal pipestem fibrosis on ultrasound, and eggs in stool.

entities.name: Tuberculoid Leprosy
entities.description: Mycobacterial skin infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae producing hypopigmented or erythematous plaques; differentiated from cutaneous leishmaniasis by complete loss of thermal and tactile sensation within lesions and thickened palpable peripheral nerves.

entities.name: Acute Leukemia and Myeloproliferative Disorders
entities.description: Malignant hematologic neoplasms presenting with splenomegaly, fever, and cytopenias; differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis by bone marrow aspirate demonstrating clonal blast populations rather than LD bodies within benign histiocytes.

entities.name: Tropical Phagedenic and Bacterial Pyogenic Ulcers
entities.description: Acute, painful, rapidly extending necrotizing dermal ulcerations caused by polymicrobial bacterial infection (fusospirochetal, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes); differentiated from cutaneous leishmaniasis by acute painful purulent onset, rapid response to beta-lactams, and lack of indolent indurated volcanic edges.

entities.name: Liposomal Amphotericin B Intravenous Monotherapy
entities.description: Global first-line antileishmanial regimen for visceral leishmaniasis; a single intravenous dose of 10 mg/kg in South Asia achieves definitive cure rates exceeding 95-98%, with rapid defervescence within 7-10 days, splenic regression, and hematologic normalization.

entities.name: Miltefosine Oral Regimen
entities.description: First oral alkylphosphocholine antileishmanial agent administered at 2.5 mg/kg/day orally for 28 days, exhibiting high efficacy in visceral and cutaneous leishmaniasis, with strict contraindication in pregnant females due to potent teratogenic risk.

entities.name: Pentavalent Antimonial Parenteral Therapy (Sodium Stibogluconate and Meglumine Antimoniate)
entities.description: Parenteral therapy at 20 mg Sb5+/kg/day IV or IM for 20-30 days effective for cutaneous, mucocutaneous, and antimonial-sensitive visceral leishmaniasis, requiring cardiac monitoring due to risks of QT interval prolongation, lethal arrhythmias, pancreatitis, and chemical hepatitis.

entities.name: Intralesional Antimonial Infiltration and Topical Paromomycin Ointment
entities.description: Local therapeutic modality for uncomplicated localized Old World cutaneous leishmaniasis, utilizing intralesional antimonial injections (1-3 mL every 3-7 days) or topical 15% paromomycin sulfate ointment to induce direct parasite membrane disintegration without systemic toxicity.

entities.name: Acquired Pentavalent Antimonial Resistance in the Bihar Endemic Focus
entities.description: Widespread parasite resistance of Leishmania donovani to sodium stibogluconate in the Bihar state of Eastern India, resulting in therapeutic failure rates exceeding 60-65% and necessitating liposomal amphotericin B or combination regimens as first-line replacements.

entities.name: Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Agent Refractoriness
entities.description: Total absence of clinical or microbiological response to standard broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (including beta-lactams, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides) despite prolonged administration for presumed bacterial sepsis or skin infection.

relationships.target: Phlebotomine Sandfly Bite
relationships.keywords: sandfly vector bite, phlebotomus, lutzomyia, dusk to dawn inoculation
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Leishmaniasis is transmitted to humans during the blood meal of infected female phlebotomine sandflies (Phlebotomus in the Old World, Lutzomyia in the New World) regurgitating metacyclic promastigotes into the dermis.

relationships.target: Endemic Visceral Leishmaniasis Geographic Exposure in South Asia and East Africa
relationships.keywords: epidemiologic travel history, kala-azar endemicity, bihar, east africa, south asia
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Visceral leishmaniasis transmission is intensely concentrated in rural agricultural areas of Eastern India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sudan, South Sudan, and Ethiopia where sandfly vectors flourish in mud dwellings.

relationships.target: Zoonotic Canine Reservoir Exposure in the Mediterranean Basin and Latin America
relationships.keywords: canine reservoir host, leishmania infantum, peri-urban zoonosis, brazil, mediterranean
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Zoonotic visceral leishmaniasis is maintained in domestic dog reservoirs, where sandflies feed on parasitized dogs and transmit Leishmania infantum to humans, particularly affecting infants and immunocompromised adults.

relationships.target: Sylvatic Forest Rodent and Marsupial Habitat Exposure in Latin America
relationships.keywords: forest reservoir host, chiclero occupation, jungle exposure, new world cutaneous leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Cutaneous and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis in the Americas is an occupational jungle zoonosis acquired when humans intrude into rainforest ecosystems where Lutzomyia sandflies feed on sylvatic rodent and marsupial reservoirs.

relationships.target: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Co-Infection and Cellular Immunosuppression
relationships.keywords: hiv coinfection, cd4 cell immunosuppression, visceral disease progression, opportunistic reactivation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] HIV co-infection and systemic immunosuppression impair Th1 cell-mediated control, transforming latent Leishmania infection into aggressive, relapsing, multi-organ visceral or diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis.

relationships.target: Leishmania donovani Species Complex
relationships.keywords: etiologic agent, visceral leishmaniasis, obligate intracellular protozoan, macrophage amastigote
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leishmaniasis in its anthroponotic visceral form is caused by Leishmania donovani, which parasitizes host mononuclear phagocytes and disseminates throughout the reticuloendothelial organs including the spleen, liver, and bone marrow.

relationships.target: Leishmania infantum (syn. Leishmania chagasi)
relationships.keywords: zoonotic visceral pathogen, leishmania infantum, leishmania chagasi, pediatric kala-azar
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leishmaniasis manifests as zoonotic visceral disease caused by Leishmania infantum (chagasi), targeting domestic dogs as primary reservoirs and causing systemic reticuloendothelial disease in humans.

relationships.target: Leishmania braziliensis Complex
relationships.keywords: mucocutaneous pathogen, viannia subgenus, espundia, metastatic mucosal dissemination
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leishmaniasis presents in destructive mucocutaneous forms primarily caused by the Leishmania braziliensis complex, which metastasizes to respiratory and oral cartilaginous structures.

relationships.target: Leishmania mexicana Complex
relationships.keywords: cutaneous chondral pathogen, chiclero ulcer, leishmania mexicana, diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leishmaniasis in Central America and Mexico is frequently caused by Leishmania mexicana, leading to indolent cutaneous lesions and mutilating auricular cartilage ulceration.

relationships.target: Leishmania major and Leishmania tropica
relationships.keywords: old world cutaneous leishmaniasis, oriental sore, leishmania major, leishmania tropica
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Leishmaniasis causes Old World cutaneous disease through Leishmania major and Leishmania tropica, producing localized granulomatous skin ulcerations at sandfly inoculation sites.

relationships.target: Massive Non-Tender Splenomegaly
relationships.keywords: massive splenomegaly, firm non-tender spleen, reticuloendothelial hyperplasia, pelvic brim spleen
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Visceral leishmaniasis is hallmarked by massive, hard, non-tender splenomegaly extending across the abdomen, resulting from profound macrophage proliferation and vascular congestion.

relationships.target: Double-Spiking Daily Fever Curve (Dromedary Fever)
relationships.keywords: dromedary fever pattern, double daily fever spike, undulating chronic fever, kala-azar fever
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Visceral leishmaniasis exhibits a characteristic dromedary fever pattern featuring two febrile spikes daily over weeks to months, contrasting with cyclic malarial paroxysms.

relationships.target: Profound Cachexia with Ashen Cutaneous Hyperpigmentation
relationships.keywords: cachexia, temporal wasting, kala-azar hyperpigmentation, black fever, protuberant abdomen
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Advanced visceral leishmaniasis causes rapid cachectic wasting alongside dark grayish-black hyperpigmentation of the face and extremities due to cytokine-mediated wasting and endocrine disturbance.

relationships.target: Volcano-Like Painless Cutaneous Ulcer with Raised Indurated Border
relationships.keywords: volcanic crater ulcer, indurated violaceous border, oriental sore, intact sensation, painless ulcer
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Cutaneous leishmaniasis manifests as an indolent volcano-like ulcer featuring raised indurated borders and a central necrotic base while preserving tactile sensation.

relationships.target: Destructive Mucocutaneous Granulomatous Ulceration with Tapir-Face Deformity
relationships.keywords: mucocutaneous espundia, septal perforation, tapir face deformity, laryngeal cartilage destruction
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis leads to irreversible cartilage necrosis and ulceration of the nasopharynx and palate, causing tapir snout deformity and airway compromise.

relationships.target: Chiclero's Auricular Chondral Ulcer
relationships.keywords: chiclero ulcer, pinna cartilage destruction, ear notch defect, leishmania mexicana
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Chiclero's ulcer is a hallmark chondral manifestation of Leishmania mexicana infection causing permanent destructive clefting of the pinna.

relationships.target: Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL)
relationships.keywords: pkdl, post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis, hypopigmented macules, nodular facial rash, reservoir host
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis presents as a diffuse macular or nodular cutaneous eruption following visceral leishmaniasis cure, serving as an important human transmission reservoir.

relationships.target: Pancytopenia with Severe Leukopenia, Anemia, and Thrombocytopenia
relationships.keywords: pancytopenia, severe leukopenia, neutropenia, normocytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, hypersplenism
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Visceral leishmaniasis consistently produces admission pancytopenia, marked by profound leukopenia (often < 2,500/uL) and thrombocytopenia resulting from bone marrow parasitization and hypersplenic sequestration.

relationships.target: Marked Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia with Reversed Albumin-to-Globulin Ratio
relationships.keywords: hypergammaglobulinemia, reversed ag ratio, polyclonal igg surge, elevated total protein, hypoalbuminemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Visceral leishmaniasis triggers immense polyclonal B-cell activation, yielding severe hypergammaglobulinemia (A:G ratio < 0.5) with total protein frequently exceeding 10 g/dL.

relationships.target: Intracellular Leishman-Donovan Amastigote Bodies in Macrophages
relationships.keywords: leishman-donovan bodies, amastigotes, kinetoplast, bone marrow aspirate, splenic smear, giemsa stain
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Microscopic demonstration of intracellular Leishman-Donovan amastigotes displaying a characteristic rod-shaped kinetoplast within macrophages on tissue aspirates represents the gold standard diagnostic pattern.

relationships.target: Positive Recombinant Kinesin Antigen rK39 Immunochromatographic Dipstick
relationships.keywords: rk39 rapid test, kinesin antigen dipstick, serological point of care, kala-azar rdt
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Visceral leishmaniasis demonstrates high-titer reactivity on the rK39 immunochromatographic dipstick test, providing rapid bed-side serological confirmation at triage.

relationships.target: Homogeneous Splenomegaly and Hepatomegaly on Bedside Ultrasound
relationships.keywords: ultrasound splenomegaly, homogeneous spleen echotexture, smooth hepatomegaly, absence of abscesses
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside abdominal ultrasound in visceral leishmaniasis reveals massive uniform splenomegaly without focal lesions, helping rule out amoebic or pyogenic splenic abscesses and echinococcal cysts.

relationships.target: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/uL)
relationships.keywords: neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated wbc, rule out visceral leishmaniasis, leukopenia requirement
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] The presence of marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/uL) strongly rules out uncomplicated visceral leishmaniasis, pointing toward acute pyogenic bacterial infection or leukemoid reaction.

relationships.target: Loss of Thermal or Pinprick Sensation within Cutaneous Skin Lesion
relationships.keywords: anesthetic skin lesion, loss of sensation, preserved cutaneous sensation, rule out cutaneous leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Loss of sensation (anesthetic patch) within a chronic skin lesion strongly rules out cutaneous leishmaniasis, which consistently maintains intact neurocutaneous sensation.

relationships.target: Circulating Leukemic Blast Cells on Peripheral Blood Smear or Bone Marrow
relationships.keywords: leukemic blasts, acute leukemia, bone marrow malignancy, rule out leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Detection of neoplastic blast cells on peripheral blood film or bone marrow aspirate rules out leishmaniasis as the primary driver of splenomegaly and pancytopenia.

relationships.target: Periportal Pipestem Fibrosis and Schistosoma Eggs on Microscopic Stool Exam
relationships.keywords: symmers pipestem fibrosis, schistosoma mansoni eggs, afebrile portal hypertension, rule out visceral leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Ultrasonographic demonstration of Symmers periportal pipestem fibrosis combined with schistosome eggs in stool confirms hepatosplenic schistosomiasis and excludes visceral leishmaniasis.

relationships.target: Intraerythrocytic Plasmodium Ring Trophozoites on Blood Smear with Indirect Hyperbilirubinemia
relationships.keywords: plasmodium intraerythrocytic ring, blood film malaria, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, rule out leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Demonstration of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium rings on Giemsa blood smear confirms acute or chronic malaria as the source of fever and splenomegaly, excluding isolated leishmaniasis.

relationships.target: Hyperreactive Malarial Splenomegaly (HMS)
relationships.keywords: hms, chronic malaria, massive splenomegaly contrast, artemisinin response, rk39 negative
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly by its double-spiking daily fevers, severe pancytopenia, marked IgG hypergammaglobulinemia, positive rK39 dipstick, and intracellular LD bodies in bone marrow macrophages.

relationships.target: Hepatosplenic Schistosomiasis
relationships.keywords: schistosomiasis contrast, pipestem fibrosis, afebrile portal hypertension, stool ova
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from hepatosplenic schistosomiasis because leishmaniasis produces unremitting high fever, profound bone marrow pancytopenia, and marrow amastigotes, whereas schistosomiasis is afebrile with preserved leukocyte counts and periportal fibrosis.

relationships.target: Tuberculoid Leprosy
relationships.keywords: leprosy differential, anesthetic patch, peripheral neuropathy, preserved sensation
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is differentiated from tuberculoid leprosy by its ulcerated volcanic morphology, completely preserved sensation within lesions, normal peripheral nerves, and presence of amastigotes rather than acid-fast bacilli on biopsy.

relationships.target: Acute Leukemia and Myeloproliferative Disorders
relationships.keywords: hematologic malignancy differential, leukemic blasts, marrow cytogenetics, ld bodies contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leishmaniasis is differentiated from acute leukemia and myeloproliferative disorders by bone marrow cytology showing histiocytes packed with Leishman-Donovan bodies and reactive polyclonal plasmacytosis rather than neoplastic blast infiltration.

relationships.target: Tropical Phagedenic and Bacterial Pyogenic Ulcers
relationships.keywords: bacterial skin ulcer differential, painful purulent ulcer, antibiotic response contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Cutaneous leishmaniasis is differentiated from bacterial pyogenic and tropical phagedenic ulcers by its indolent, painless chronic evolution, raised indurated borders, refractory response to antibacterial agents, and presence of intracellular amastigotes on edge scraping.

relationships.target: Liposomal Amphotericin B Intravenous Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: first-line visceral therapy, liposomal amphotericin b, ambisome single dose, 95 percent cure rate
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Visceral leishmaniasis responds rapidly to intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (single dose of 10 mg/kg in South Asia or multi-dose regimens in East Africa), achieving >95% cure and prompt resolution of fever and splenomegaly.

relationships.target: Miltefosine Oral Regimen
relationships.keywords: oral antileishmanial, miltefosine, 28-day regimen, teratogenic contraindication
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Leishmaniasis responds to oral miltefosine (2.5 mg/kg/day for 28 days), which achieves high cure rates for visceral leishmaniasis and Old/New World cutaneous leishmaniasis, provided strict pregnancy prevention is maintained.

relationships.target: Pentavalent Antimonial Parenteral Therapy (Sodium Stibogluconate and Meglumine Antimoniate)
relationships.keywords: pentavalent antimonials, sodium stibogluconate, meglumine antimoniate, qt prolongation risk
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Antimonial-sensitive strains of Leishmania respond to parenteral sodium stibogluconate or meglumine antimoniate (20 mg Sb5+/kg/day for 20-30 days), though monitored for cardiotoxicity and pancreatitis.

relationships.target: Intralesional Antimonial Infiltration and Topical Paromomycin Ointment
relationships.keywords: intralesional antimonials, topical paromomycin, localized cutaneous therapy, membrane disruption
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Uncomplicated localized cutaneous leishmaniasis responds favorably to intralesional pentavalent antimonial infiltration or topical paromomycin ointment, inducing accelerated ulcer healing without systemic toxicity.

relationships.target: Acquired Pentavalent Antimonial Resistance in the Bihar Endemic Focus
relationships.keywords: antimonial drug resistance, bihar kala-azar failure, sodium stibogluconate unresponsiveness
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Visceral leishmaniasis strains in the hyperendemic focus of Bihar, India exhibit extensive acquired resistance to pentavalent antimonials (failure rates >60-65%), precluding their empirical use in this region.

relationships.target: Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Agent Refractoriness
relationships.keywords: antibiotic refractoriness, beta-lactam failure, fluoroquinolone unresponsiveness, diagnostic clue
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Leishmaniasis is intrinsically refractory to standard broad-spectrum antibacterial agents (beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, macrolides), providing a critical diagnostic clue when prolonged febrile or ulcerative illness fails to respond to empiric antibiotic courses.
